scope: Proposition 2.4 (Canonical drift) of the manuscript “The free uniform spanning forest is a factor of IID” (preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 231 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 478f5137621e0b3b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Each be is a jointly Borel function on [0, ∞)×RE with values in [0, 1], where RE has its product Borel structure. The construction commutes with graph isomorphisms and does not select a root. For every t ≥ 0 and y, y′ ∈ RE such that supf∈E |yf − y′ f | < ∞, it satisfies sup e∈E |be(t, y) − be(t, y′ )| ≤ 1 2 sup f∈E |yf − y′ f |. (2.10) Neither y nor y′ is required to have bounded coordinates.
